WPSS No. 2112 of 2019

Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate, for the 
petitioner. 
Mrs. Anjali Bhargava, Addl. C.S.C. for the 
State of Uttarakhand. 
Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate, assisted by 
Mr. Vinay Bhatt, Advocate, for respondent Nos. 2 
and 3. 
These are bunch of four Writ Petitions. 
Learned counsel for the petitioner of Writ 
Petition Nos. 2111 of 2019, submits that the issue 
involved in this Writ Petition happens to be akin to 
the issue involved in Writ Petition No. 2112 of 
2019. 
Hence, both these Writ Petitions are 
connected. 
The other Writ Petitions, i.e. WPSS Nos. 
1945 of 2019 and 790 of 2020, deal with altogether 
a different issue. These Writ Petitions are directed 
to be dis-connected from the bunch of Writ 
Petitions, i.e. WPSS No. 2111 of 2019 and 2112 of 
2019. 
In the meantime, the learned counsel for the 
petitioner in Writ Petition No. 790 of 2020, would 
comply the order of 27th October, 2021, of placing 
on record the additional documents, which he 
intended to file. 
Put up these Writ Petitions in the week 
commencing 27th December, 2021. 
Interim order, if any, would continue to 
operate till the next date of listing. 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 01.12.2021
Shiv

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 2111 of 2019
With
WPSS No. 2112 of 2019
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel 
for the petitioner.
2. Mr. R.C. Joshi, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State.
3. Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Mr. Shravan 
Pandey, learned counsel for respondent 
nos. 2 and 3.
4. In both the petitions, the 
petitioners are claiming compassionate 
appointment on the ground that their
husband who was serving in sugar 
factory as daily wagers since 1989,
without any break, died in harness. 
5. It is submitted that after death of 
the husbands of the petitioners, 
respondent offered appointment to 
both the petitioners on contractual 
basis on consolidated salary and since 
then they are continuing. 
6. Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior 
Advocate for the respondents seeks 
time to verify whether there was any
break in service of the deceased 
employee. 
7. Put up this mater for final disposal 
on 25.11.2024 immediately after fresh.
8. In the meantime, since the 
petitioners are serving as sweepers,  the respondents are directed either to 
pay regular pay as attached to the post 
of the sweeper or to show cause on the 
date fixed.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 17.10.2024
Parul
